mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS change is not above 0.25% in any observed window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength boosts equity sentiment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the PAYEMS threshold being met (p < 0.05), or the effect is not significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1250 units in a month, it indicates robust consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 20 test windows, the 5-day forward return is not positive when HOUST crosses 1250 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing signals economic weakness.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative during the INDPRO decline (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent in out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment) by at least 0.5% and 0.2% respectively over 3 months triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via risk-off to risk-on shift.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month - 0.5% AND UNRATE < previous month - 0.2% over 3 months
regime_hint: Dual risk-off signals (rate hike expectations + falling unemployment)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the interaction trigger (p > 0.05), or proxies do not meet the threshold in any observed window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it suggests labor market tightening, which is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return in a growth regime.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening in expansion phase
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during the trigger (p > 0.05), or the effect is not statistically significant out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's values by at least 2% each predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to strong aggregate demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month + 2% AND RSAFS > previous month + 2%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies exceed thresholds (p > 0.05), or interaction effect is not detected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of 0.3% or more for three consecutive months indicates persistent inflation pressure, which is linked to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous month - 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the CPI decline (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent in out-of-sample testing.
